Print or query a figure's subplot grid

Source: R/subplots.R
print_grid.Rd

print_grid() prints the layout of a grid created by make_subplots(). get_subplot() returns the layout object(s) of one grid cell: a list with xaxis and yaxis for 2D cartesian subplots, the scene, polar, etc. object for other subplot types, or the x and y domain for "domain" subplots.

Usage

print_grid(fig)

get_subplot(fig, row, col, secondary_y = FALSE)

Arguments

fig

A figure created by make_subplots().

row, col

Grid cell (1-based).

secondary_y

If TRUE, the cell's secondary y axis.

Value

print_grid() returns fig invisibly; get_subplot() returns the subplot's layout objects, or NULL for an empty cell.

Examples

fig <- make_subplots(rows = 2, cols = 2, specs = list(
  list(list(), list(type = "polar")),
  list(list(colspan = 2), NULL)
))
print_grid(fig)
#> This is the format of your plot grid:
#> [ (1,1) x,y   ]  [ (1,2) polar ]
#> [ (2,1) x2,y2           -      ]
get_subplot(fig, 1, 2)
#> <go_layout_polar>
#> {
#>   "domain": {
#>     "x": [
#>       0.55,
#>       1
#>     ],
#>     "y": [
#>       0.575,
#>       1
#>     ]
#>   }
#> }
#>
